reason: E1 directly supports friction and wear reduction and the MoO2 mechanism, but only for a nitride coating, not a bulk HEA. E2 does not address tribological properties or MoO2 formation. The hypothesis overstates the evidence by extrapolating from a coating to a bulk alloy and from unspecified Mo content to 10-12 at.%.
premises: Mo addition to HEA reduces friction coefficient from ~0.7 to ~0.26
Mo addition to HEA reduces wear rate by an order of magnitude
Friction reduction is due to formation of layered MoO2 tribolayer
Wear reduction is due to combined hardness and toughness from MoO2
These effects are achievable with 10-12 at.% Mo in a bulk HEA
